title: How Much You Should Have Saved by Age 35 Based on U.S. Income Benchmarks
description: Data-driven milestones for net worth and liquid savings in your mid-30s.
content:
Age 35 is a financial checkpoint. You are likely a decade into your career, potentially hitting peak earning years, but also facing peak expenses (homes, kids). It is the moment where compound interest shifts from a 'nice to have' to a 'must have'. If you are behind at 35, catching up is possible but requires drastic action. If you are ahead, you are on the path to early independence. This guide provides specific multiples of income you should aim for based on data from Fidelity and US averages.

Key Takeaways

  • The 1.5x to 2x Rule: Most financial planners suggest having 1.5 to 2 times your annual salary saved for retirement by age 35. If you earn $100k, aim for $150k-$200k invested.
  • Liquid Liquidity: Apart from retirement, you should have 6 months of cash expenses. At 35, the risk of layoff or home repair is higher than at 25.
  • Net Worth vs. Invested Assets: Do not confuse home equity with retirement savings. You can't eat your house. Focus on 'Invested Assets' for this benchmark.
  • The Catch-Up Math: If you have $0 at 35, you need to save ~25% of your income to retire at 65. The 10% rule is gone for you.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The median US net worth for those under 35 is relatively low due to student loans. However, to maintain a middle-class lifestyle in retirement without relying solely on Social Security, you must aim for the average of successful savers, not the national median.

The Benchmarks by Income

Where should you be? Compare yourself to the target, not the peer group.

Salary: $75,000

  • Target Net Worth: $110,000 - $150,000.
  • Breakdown: ~$100k in 401(k)/IRA + ~$15k Cash.
  • Reality: This requires maxing an IRA ($7k) and getting the 401(k) match since age 25.

Salary: $150,000 (High Earner)

  • Target Net Worth: $250,000 - $300,000.
  • Why higher multiple? Social Security replaces less of your income. You need to self-fund more of your lifestyle.
  • Reality: You should have been maxing your 401(k) ($23k) for the last 5-7 years.

The 'Behind' Scenario

If you have $20k at age 35, don't panic. But realize that 'Compound Interest' can no longer do all the heavy lifting. 'Savings Rate' must take over. You need to cut expenses to save $1,500+ month immediately.

How to Accelerate at 35

  1. Avoid the 'Forever Home' Trap: Many 35-year-olds buy too much house, diverting cash flow to mortgage interest. Buy a smaller house or keep renting to keep liquidity high.
  2. The 'Dual Income' Supercharge: If you have a partner, try to live on one salary and save the other entirely. This catches you up in 3-4 years.
  3. Career Pivot: Your income at 35 dictates your saving capacity. If you are underpaid, switching jobs often yields a 15-20% raise. Loyalty is expensive.
  4. Audit Fees: You have a real portfolio now. Ensure you aren't paying 1% fees. Switching to low-cost index funds saves you thousands over the next 30 years.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does home equity count?

For Net Worth, yes. For the '2x Salary' retirement benchmark, no. You can't spend your house in retirement unless you sell it. Focus on liquid assets.

What if I have kids?

Kids slow down savings. That's normal. Don't stop contributing to the 401(k) match, even if daycare costs are high. The free money is essential.

Is it too late to FIRE?

No. Starting at 35, you can retire at 50 or 55 if you save 40-50%. You just missed the 'Easy FIRE' window of starting at 22.
